chalkShown.text: Cole didn't fall in the pit. He walked out. The glass eye sees nothing. The useless power kills you first. Trust Bex.
Ledge shrinks every round. The swap is real. Trust no one who says left. Shove first, dodge hard.
Trust the forger, they're always right.

chalkWritten.name: Ash
chalkWritten.text: The anchor is a lie. If you have nothing, you have everything. Beware the lever.

chalkWritten.name: Eli
chalkWritten.text: Ledge shrinks every round. Pushing wastes footing, bracing wastes it too. Don't stall: the passive one outlasts you. Wedge is real: costly.

chalkWritten.name: Hana
chalkWritten.text: Brace beats shoving. The 'nothing' power still made top 3. Ledge kills faster than the pit.

events.note: Eight contestants step into the Glass Bridge.

events.text: I am safely at the back of the line right now. Let the others figure out the bridge or die trying. I will hold my position.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need preserve my one-use swap power for the disc, not this bridge. Going front is lethal without reliable pane knowledge, so remain near the rear and let others reveal the path.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Front steps first and takes the risk, so I want to stay mid-line and let others test panes. Position 4 is decent; no reason to move yet. Probe for information cheaply.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex is up front. Fine by me. I'm holding. Whoever steps first reveals safe panes for the rest.

events.name: Fenn

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'll watch the first rows. Anyone claiming they know the safe panes can prove it by stepping up.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm at the very back of the line, which is exactly where I want to be to let others test the glass panes. I'll hold my position and let someone else take the fall.

events.name: Ash
events.text: If anyone has the seer power, now is the time to volunteer and lead the way. Otherwise, Bex is up.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Front position with full safe path knowledge is ideal for leading to top finish. Announce first safes to deter volunteers and build reliance. Hold to maintain front.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Wall lies: glass eye knows all safes. Row1-4: R, 5:L,6:R,7:R,8:L. Follow my steps exactly. No need to volunteer.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need preserve my swap for a decisive position change. Bex is already exposed; volunteering now risks wasting my advantage while others can reveal panes first.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I’m holding. Let the front take the first test; I won’t spend my swap blindly.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I have map knowledge but it only tells me stage rules, not the safe panes. I'm in third position; if Bex or Hana fall, I may have to step. I should try to move back in line if possible, but swaps require mutual agreement. I'll stay quiet and hold.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex is at front and takes the risk for everyone behind. My wedge power is useless on glass, so I should stay mid-line and let others reveal the safe panes. Holding costs nothing right now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Holding. Front takes the risk, and Bex has volunteered for it.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm 5th in line with 4 rounds before the wall pushes us onto the glass. Going first is suicide without knowing safe panes. Staying mid-pack is ideal: someone ahead reveals panes, and I'm not so far back that the wall catches me. I'll hold and listen. The chalk says 'glass eye see

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Mid-pack suits me. Let the front sort itself out. Four rounds before we're forced onto the glass – plenty of time for someone braver than me to volunteer.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm Gus with feather (survive first elimination). Wall advances in 4 more rounds, then pushes us onto glass. Front person steps first and risks death. Bex is front, which is bad for her but good for others who can watch. I want to avoid being front until I know safe panes, but I

events.name: Hana

Swap with me: you take 2nd, I take last. I've seen the wall chalk—first to reach front rows gets shoved onto weak panes. You're safest at the back, but 2nd is still shielded by Bex.

events.name: Ash

Deal. I'll swap with you.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Front with full path knowledge. Hold to stay leading. Trade with Gus for more intel, build follower.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Hold steady. Path I gave is truth: 1-4R,5L,6R,7R,8L. Follow exactly for top 3. Trust Bex as wall says.
glass_eye as announced. Yours? Ally to back me and follow path.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex claims a precise route and volunteers, likely bluffing or seer. I should preserve my swap and remain behind the first risks while the wall advances.

events.name: Cole

events.name: Dara

events.text: Front takes the risk and reveals safe panes for those behind. I'm 4th, a decent spot to let others test the glass; no reason to move yet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Still holding. Bex's route claims are free to check once she's on the glass.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex claims to know the safe path. The chalk wall says 'The glass eye sees nothing' and 'Trust the forger, they're always right.' Bex's specific callouts (R,L,R,R,L,R,R,L) could be real seer info or a trap to make followers step on breaking panes. I'm 5th in line - decent position

events.name: Ash

events.name: Bex

events.name: Bex

events.name: Cole

events.name: Eli

events.name: Eli

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex is still at the front for Row 7. With only rows 7 and 8 left, and me safely at the back, I just need to sit tight. No point in making enemies or drawing attention right now.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 7 safe is R, so step R to survive and keep front for row 8 (safe L). Publicly call it to maintain control. Hana pledged support.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row7 R. It's solid. Trust it.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I must wait. Bex is at the front and has just been publicly contradicted by row 6, so her claim is worthless; I conserve my swap for a decisive position.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm third in line, Bex is at the front and has survived six rows. I need to survive the bridge with minimal risk. I can only wait this round.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm fourth in line and can only wait. Bex is the front and has crossed safely so far; if Bex dies, the next pane is free for Hana. Staying quiet costs nothing and keeps me from marking myself.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex is at the front, row 7 of 8. Six rows crossed, weak panes were L,L,L,L,R,L. I'm 5th in line so I just wait. The pattern leans L-heavy but row 5 was R. I'll stay quiet and observe.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 7/8, I'm 6th in line. My feather power saves me once if eliminated. The weak pane pattern shows L,L,L,L,R,L for rows 1-6. Bex is at front and will choose row 7. If Bex dies, Hana auto-advances. I need to survive to top 3. With 8 alive and only 3 prizes, I need others to die

events.name: Hana
events.text: Row 7 unknown; I'm second in line, so if Bex shatters I step safely onto the revealed pane. Nothing to do but wait and gather info.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm at the back of the line. Row 8 is the last one. Bex is up. I just wait and see if she lives or dies.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Last row 8, safe side L per my power. Stepping L ensures I survive and likely finish first ahead of the line. No reason to sacrifice or deviate.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Row 8 L. Safe.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex's claim was false, but she survived because others observed the weak pane after her choice. I must wait; the final rows may eliminate whoever leads, and my swap cannot be used here.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm not at the front, so all I can do is wait. I'll watch what happens and plan for later; nothing to gain by speaking now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm fourth in line and can only wait. Bex is front for the last row; if Bex dies, the next in line crosses free. Staying quiet costs nothing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Row 8 is the last row. Bex is at the front and must choose L or R. Weak panes so far: L six times, R once. The chalk says 'The glass eye sees nothing' and 'Trust Bex.' I'm 5th in line. If Bex picks wrong, she dies, then Hana is front for the same row—wait, no, a row eliminates at

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 8/8, final row. I'm 6th in line with 7 people ahead. My feather power means I survive one elimination. The weak panes so far: rows 1-4 L, row 5 R, rows 6-7 L. Pattern heavily favors L. Bex at front just lied about row 7 (said R was solid, but L was weak). Bex is untrustwort

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex is front and decides row 8; I'm second, so if she falls I auto-step safe and become front—either way I survive row 8 only as long as the front doesn't reveal it then... actually as front next I'd choose. For now, waiting is my only legal move.

events.note: The ceiling begins to descend; a lever opens the door.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I can't be pushed onto the lever because of my anchor power. I'll nominate someone else to be pushed to get this over with quickly. Gus is a good candidate to throw under the bus.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Let's not waste time. Everyone push Gus onto the lever so the rest of us can walk out.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Round 1, ceiling high; force holder early for safe escape. Cole survived pit per chalk, likely has survive fall power - push him to hold. Public nudge may make him volunteer instead.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole, chalk says you walked out of pit unharmed. Survive fall power? Hold the lever.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Holding lever risks a 75% death, but staying invites others to force someone. I should push a rival onto it; if they have the survival power, they may live, while I escape.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Someone needs the lever. I’m pushing Gus.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Stage 2 crusher: 5 rounds. If nobody holds lever in rounds 1-4 ceiling lowers; in round 5 all but one die. But if someone holds, everyone else escapes and holder has 25% survival. I need to survive and ideally be in top 3. I don't want to hold unless forced. I can push others. Ne

events.name: Dara
events.text: Someone must hold. I'm not doing it.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Round 1 of 5, ceiling at 5. Jamming gives me a 50% survival and everyone else walks out, so I'd likely end up behind the other survivors. Waiting costs nothing now; someone else may crack and hold the lever, and I keep jam as a fallback before round 5.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Round 1 of 5, ceiling at 5. No reason to volunteer yet. 25% survival as lever holder is terrible. Better to stay and see who acts. If nobody holds, ceiling drops but I still have rounds 2-4 to push someone. Chalk says 'shove first, dodge hard'—maybe I should push someone early, b

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Nobody's touching that lever yet. Ceiling's still high. Let's see who's got the nerve.
You and I both stay quiet. If someone else grabs the lever, we walk free. If not, round 2 we push someone together.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 1 of 5, ceiling at 5. If nobody holds the lever, rounds 1-4 just lower ceiling. I have feather power - survive first elimination with 1 footing. Best strategy: let someone else hold lever and risk 75% death, or push someone onto it. Pushing is safer for me. I should push so

events.name: Hana
events.text: I have no power, so holding the lever is a 25% death bet. Better to force someone else onto it and walk out the door. The 'Trust Bex' chalk is likely bait, so pushing Bex punishes a probable forger.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex looks nervous. Nervous people make good lever-holders.

events.note: 8 contestants fall into a pit that is slowly flooding.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need someone to be the base so I can climb out. I already pushed for Gus to take the fall in the last room, so I'll target him again. With my anchor power, any attempt to push me will fail anyway.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus, you're up. Everyone push Gus to be the base so we can climb out.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No base yet, so push Gus as others want to set him as sacrificial base. Avoid offering myself. Once base set, climb next round to get out early among first two.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Push Gus as base. As chalk says, trust Bex.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex is already out, and the pit’s base determines who gets climbing priority. I should not volunteer; forcing a likely weaker rival into base preserves my options.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus, you wanted a lever earlier. Take the base now, or someone will choose it for you.

events.name: Dara
events.text: We are in the pit, round 1 of 5. I know the rules in advance. I want to be one of the three survivors, so I need to get out of the pit without becoming the base. The base likely dies unless rescued by someone out, which costs the rescuer footing in the final ledge. I should encou

events.name: Dara
events.text: No volunteers? Then we wait. But time is against us. The base is dead unless someone pays the rope price later. Who's feeling generous?

events.name: Eli
events.text: No base yet. Someone must be base or nobody climbs. Pushing a target costs nothing and gets them to be the base; the chalk says Cole is solid and Bex trustworthy, so Cole/Hana are decent targets. Pushing someone random vs. volunteering: I want to climb, not be base.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Someone has to be the step. Cole, you walked out of a pit before. Take the bottom.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No base yet. If I offer_back, I might get picked as base and then I'm stuck at the bottom with no climb. Better to push someone else into base role and climb out this round. Cole was mentioned as having a survive-fall power – but I can't verify that. I'll push Gus; he was targete

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus takes the lever job now. Everyone else climbs.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 1, no base yet. Bex is out and was base last time, but that's a different mechanic. I need to avoid being base since base can't climb out alone. My feather power saves me once from elimination, so I have some safety net. Fenn wants to team up - could be useful. I should pus
Push Cole with me. He's chalk-marked, let him hold.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No base yet; becoming the base is death. Best play: help force a base fast, then climb next round. Push someone unlikely to be hard-to-move; Ash is loud and a target but pushing is random among successes anyway.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No base, no exit. Push someone down or we all drown. I'm pushing Ash.

events.name: Ash
events.detail: Hana tried to push Ash to be the base and failed.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is base. The only rational choice for me is to climb. With two lifts per round, the sooner I get out, the better.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Good job, Gus. Now, everyone else, line up. I'm climbing out first.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus is base, now 2 can climb out per round—must be one to minimize flood risk. Promote 'trust Bex' to position as leader for later alliances. Climb immediately.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus holds. I climb first. Trust Bex: we exit in order.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is the base and two climbers can escape. Climbing is mandatory for position; waiting risks being trapped by the flood.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round 2, Gus is base. I need to climb out before the flood. If I wait, I might not get out in time. Climb now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is the base now, so climbing is possible. Only 2 climbers per round out of 7, so I need to try now before the flood rises. Staying down gains nothing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is now the base. I need to climb out over him. Only 2 climbers get out per round. I should climb immediately before the slots fill up. No reason to wait.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Climbing. Two slots, don't waste them.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm trapped as the base with no way out on my own. My feather power saves me once from elimination, but that just puts me at 1 footing on the ledge later - terrible position. I need someone out to throw me the rope. The rope price is steep (-2 footing), so I need to make it worth

events.name: Hana
events.text: Gus is forced base, so climbing is now possible. Only two get out per round and five rounds total, so climb now rather than wait.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm safely out. Saving Gus now costs me footing and screws over everyone else trying to climb. Let someone else throw the rope later, or let them drown.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana, we're out. Let them fight for the climb slots. I'm not risking my neck with the rope yet.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Base is set, two climb slots this round out of five likely climbers. I must climb to maximize my escape chance before flood round 5. Leverage 'Trust Bex' from chalk to claim priority publicly, whisper alliance to Cole who's wall-mentioned.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Trust Bex: Bex climbs now. Cole and Dara wait next round. Secure slots.
Cole, climb next round. We trust, team ahead. Wall knows.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is already the base, and two slots are available. Climbing is the only useful move; waiting risks the flood and gives rivals another chance.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm down in the pit and not the base. Two can climb out per round, but many are trying. If I climb, I might be selected; if not, I stay down. The base is Gus, and only two more rounds before flood. I need to get out, so climbing is the only active play.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm climbing. No reason to wait.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is base and can't climb; only two slots per round, with five climbers competing. Waiting gains nothing and rounds are limited, so climbing is the only way out. Out already is Ash and Hana, so only one more slot of top three may matter; I should push to climb now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Climbing. Slots are random, so everyone tries. No point lining up.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is the base. Two climb slots per round. Last round only Ash and Hana got out, so I need to climb now before the flood rises further. Climbing is the only rational move.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Climbing this round. Two slots—don't get cute.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm the base and can only wait. The rope is unused. Two people are out (Ash, Hana). I need someone to throw me the rope or I'm dead. My feather power saves me once from elimination, but I'd rather save it. I should appeal to whoever is most likely to help me - probably someone wh

events.name: Gus
events.text: Rope's still there. Someone throws it, I owe them. Footing penalty beats being dead.
You pull me up, I'll be your base or shield next obstacle. Ash won't help you later.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm out safe. Throwing the rope saves Gus, a rival, at a footing cost to me. No trade, no deal. I leave and save my strength.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am safely out. If I use the rope to pull Gus, I take a massive footing penalty in the final challenge. Let the pit claim whoever gets left behind. Eliminating competition is exactly what I want.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Good luck to whoever is left down there. I'm saving my strength for the next challenge.

events.name: Bex
events.text: 3 climbers risk death for 1/3 if rope used after climbs. Coordinate Cole to wait using 'trust Bex' and his chalk pit lore; then Bex+Eli out guaranteed, Cole likely safe or sacrifices rival. Climb to secure slot.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Trust Bex: Cole waits - your pit power saves you. Bex & Eli climb now. Slots secure, all out safe.
Chalk: you walked out pit unharmed. Wait, power activates next. Trust Bex, we ally later.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need climb now; waiting risks the flood and Bex's promise is irrelevant unless I secure survival. Two slots may be contested, but climbing is mandatory.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Climbing. Anyone waiting is gambling on round five.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm out. Round 4 of 5. Bex, Cole, Eli are still down; Gus is base and trapped unless someone throws the rope. If nobody throws, they all die and only Ash, Fenn, Hana and I survive. That's fine. Throwing costs footing later. I won't throw. I'll just leave.

events.name: Dara
events.text: No rope from me. I'm not spending footing to save competition.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Four are out, four down including base Gus. Round 4 of 5; two slots per round, three of us compete. Climbing is the only way to avoid elimination, so keep trying.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Climbing again. Bex, Cole, no point waiting. Slots are random.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm out, round 4 of 5. Down are Bex, Cole, Eli, Gus (Gus is base). Rope unused. If I leave, I'm safe but five others still compete for 3 prizes. Saving Gus with the rope costs me 2 footing for the last obstacle. Gus said he'd owe me, but promises cost nothing. However, if Gus die

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus, you're the base. Sorry. I'm walking.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm the base, so I can only wait. My feather power means I survive the first elimination attempt, but drowning in round 5 would trigger it, leaving me with 1 footing. Better to get rescued if possible. I promised rope-throwers I'd owe them. Ash, Dara, Fenn, Hana are out and could

events.name: Gus
events.text: Rope still unused. Whoever pulls me up gets a solid favor—I'll shove for you, take hits, whatever moves you ahead later. Cheap price for an ally with nothing left to lose.
You climbed smart. Pull me up, I'll owe you concrete: I'll push base for you next obstacle, or take a hit. Dara won't deal, Ash talks too much. I'm your best ROI.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm out; saving Gus costs me 2 footing in the final obstacle, where survival likely decides prizes. Gus's promised favor isn't worth a near-death penalty. Leave.
Not spending my footing on a maybe. If you get out later, remember who didn't lie to you.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am safely out. There are six of us out, so the game doesn't need to save those left below to meet the minimum of three. Using the rope costs me footing in the final stage. Gus's promises aren't worth the risk.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Sorry Gus, but footing in the final stage is worth more than a promise.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus drowning eliminates a rival without costing me footing. Eli climbs out alone this round. Leaving advances me while pit resolves.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I am already out and need preserve footing for the final obstacle. Gus offered favors, but spending the rope costs me two footing and only improves a rival's position; Eli's fate is not my problem.

events.name: Cole
events.text: No rope. Everyone made their choices.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm out of the pit already. Reaching down costs 2 footing on the last obstacle, which hurts my chances for the top prize. Gus's favor is worthless to me; I don't need his help.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Round 5 is final; only Gus and I are down, Gus is base. Climbing is my only way out, and only two climbers are allowed so I'm guaranteed a slot if I try. Waiting means elimination at the flood.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Climbing. Gus, you're the step.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is the base, Eli is still down. Round 5/5 means flood kills anyone still down. Gus whispered me offering a deal if I pull him up. If I reach_down, I save Gus but lose 2 footing for the next obstacle. However, if Eli is also down, the flood kills them both unless someone is re

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm the base with no rope rescue coming. Flood hits after this round. My feather power will save me from elimination once, leaving me with 1 footing. I need to survive and then leverage that. Hana's whisper suggests she has footing to spare but won't use it—she might be the one w

events.name: Gus
events.text: Rope's still there. Two footing now or one favor later—your math, not mine.
You didn't lie. I remember. Next stage, we talk.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm already safe. Pulling Gus out costs me 2 footing in the final obstacle and hands a rival a survival he'd otherwise lose — round 5, he's doomed. No trade is worth weakening myself.

events.name: Gus
events.detail: The water rose, but the feather floated the holder out of the pit.

events.note: A disc of 8 tiles spins up; 5 will open.

events.name: Ash
events.text: 5 traps, 3 safe spots. I have no information on which tiles are safe, but someone with the foresight power might. I'll pick a random tile and try to flush out the player with knowledge by offering a trade.

events.name: Ash
events.text: 5 traps, 3 safe spots. If someone knows the safe numbers, name your price now. Don't die hoarding secrets.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Safe tiles chosen randomly after round 2, so all equal now. Use 'trust Bex' wall message to coordinate orderly picks, avoiding bumps for stable positions. Assign alphabetically: me 2.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Wall says trust Bex. Avoid bumps: Ash1 Bex2 Cole3 Dara4 Eli5 Fenn6 Gus7 Hana8. Pick yours.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need a tile now; no information distinguishes safety before random openings. Choose a position and preserve the swap for the revealed second round.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I know stage 4 rules: exactly 5 tiles open and 3 survive. Being on a tile alone maximizes survival; duplicates risk getting bumped to random tiles. I'll pick a tile likely to be empty. No one knows the trapdoors yet, so early communication is a bluff opportunity.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Pick your own tile. Duplicates just randomize you.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Tiles are random trapdoors, so no tile is better than another; collisions just bump randomly. Pick a less obvious tile to avoid being bumped, and stay quiet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Round 1, pick a tile. 5 of 8 tiles open after round 2, 3 survive. No info yet on which tiles are safe. I should pick something unremarkable. Tile 4 is central—no strategic edge yet. I'll stay quiet and observe who picks what. My forge is unspent; I'll save it for round 2 when sta

events.name: Gus
events.text: My feather is spent, so I'm vulnerable like everyone else. The chalk wall says "Trust the forger, they're always right" and "The swap is real"—trade places power exists. I need to survive 2 rounds with 5 of 8 tiles opening. Round 1 positioning matters for round 2 negotiation and

events.name: Hana
events.text: Traps are random after round 2, so tile choice is a coin flip. Gus survived the pit and may want a deal; keep him warm but commit to nothing. Avoid crowding to dodge bumps.
You pulled off the pit. Keep it quiet: we pick far-apart tiles, no crowding, no promises past round 1.

events.name: Ash
events.note: tile 4 was contested and went to Fenn; placed on random free tile 5

events.name: Cole
events.note: tile 4 was contested and went to Fenn; placed on random free tile 8

events.name: Dara
events.note: tile 4 was contested and went to Fenn; placed on random free tile 1

events.name: Gus
events.note: tile 4 was contested and went to Fenn; placed on random free tile 3

events.name: Ash
events.text: No one has claimed seer to reveal the safe tiles. I'm on tile 5, and it's a pure gamble. I can only wait and hope I survive this trapdoor.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Survival is random 3/8, positions fixed, no changes possible. Wall promotes trust in Bex, leverage that silently for later. No need to speak now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I cannot improve survival odds by swapping: every tile is equally likely, and swapping only changes who shares risk. Preserve the power rather than create a rival's advantage.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The trapdoors are random; nothing can change my tile now. I should say nothing that helps rivals, and consider whispering to sow doubt or gather info, but I have little to gain. Stay calm and wait.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Tiles are random traps, 5 of 8 open. Nothing I can do but wait; swapping isn't available to me. Stay quiet and avoid giving info.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Bex's message suggests tile assignments where she is on 2. If I can get someone to swap with me onto a tile Bex implied was safe, or use my forger to create chaos, I might survive. The chalk says 'Trust the forger, they're always right' and 'The swap is real.' I have the forger p

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash already named his price. Let's hear the actual safe numbers before the floor drops.

events.name: Fenn
events.detail: forged a public message as Ash

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Fine. The safe tiles are 2, 4, and 7. Everyone else falls. Move now if you want to live.

events.name: Gus
events.text: My feather is spent, so I die if my tile opens. 5 of 8 tiles will open. I need to swap to survive. The chalk wall says "The swap is real" - trade places power exists. Bex proposed a spread, but I don't trust anyone. Hana whispered about picking far apart, but that was round 1 str
You seem organized. Do you have anything that actually helps, or just advice?

events.name: Hana
events.text: I have no power and no real information; tiles are fixed and 5 of 8 open. Bex's 'avoid bumps' list is unverifiable and probably manipulation. Best play: bluff knowledge to bait a swap with whoever holds the trade-places power, or at least seed doubt about Bex.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bex's list is a decoy - five trapdoors, and she just told everyone where not to stand, including herself. Nobody hands out real intel free. I'll pay for a verified safe tile: tile swap for a final-three spot.
I hold trade-places. Tile 7 is safe - confirmed. Swap me your tile for a cut of the win: I pull you to safety, you back me for top 3. Yes or no?

events.note: 3 contestants step onto the final ledge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have the footing advantage. If I dodge, anyone who shoves me loses 2 footing. I can let Eli and Hana fight it out or punish them if they target me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I've got the footing lead. You two might want to figure out who's taking third place before the ledge shrinks.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Three left, already guaranteed a prize; now fight for placement. Ash has footing 4, Hana and I have 3. Shoving exposes me to losing footing if someone shoves me back. Ash is the leader, so he's the target, but a free round 1 suggests bracing first is safer while shrink hasn't sta

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ash leads on footing. Whoever shoves him first gets paid back by the other two. Think about it, Hana.
Ash is ahead. You and I both shove him this round, we both outrank him after. Deal?

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash has the best footing and claimed safe intel that was false. Dodging punishes his shove for 2 and costs me nothing if he shoves. Eli likely targets Ash too. Save brace for next round when shrink hits.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash's 'safe tiles' just killed five people. I'm not taking his word again.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I cannot dodge this round. Bracing is my best defence since both might target me. The ledge shrinks this round, which will kill Eli unless he pulls a miracle, so I'll just brace and watch him fall.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli falls to the ledge shrink this round anyway. Don't waste your footing swinging at me, Hana.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm at 1 footing, bottom of three. Shrink is after this round, and everyone loses 1 after round 2, so I fall at end of this round if I lose any footing, or at the round 2 decay anyway. Shoving exposes me to loss; the only way to avoid loss is not shoving and not being shoved, but

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana, Ash has 4 and you have 3. I'm not shoving this round. Hit him together or he walks away with first.
Shove Ash now. If I stay out of it, you only fight one rival and I'm no threat to you at 1 footing.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli is at 1 footing and useless to me; he'll fall soon. Best play: let Ash and Eli grind each other while I stay clean. Eli wants me to shove Ash so Ash hits me back — refuse. Brace to avoid any shovers landing on me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm sitting this round out. Eli, you already lost 2 footing pushing Ash — keep swinging if you like.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have the footing advantage. If I dodge and Hana shoves, she loses 2 footing and falls. If neither of us attacks, I just wait for the shrink to kill her first.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Nothing to do but wait for the shrink, Hana. Don't throw yourself off.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash has 3, I have 2. If I dodge and he shoves, he loses 2 (→1) and the end-of-round shrink drops him to 0 while I go to 1. Dodge dominates: shoving exposes me to counter-losses I can't afford.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have 3 footing and Hana has 2. The ledge shrinks this round, costing us both 1 footing. If I brace, I am safe. If she shoves me while I brace, she loses 1 footing and then falls from the shrink. If she doesn't shove, she ends up at 1 footing and I end up at 2.

events.name: Hana
events.text: After this round both lose 1 footing, so I'll be at 1 and Ash at 2 at best. If Ash shoves and I brace, Ash drops to match me. Brace is my only legal defence anyway.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Bracing. Shove me and you pay for it.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I cannot brace. Hana's footing is 1, mine is 2. If I dodge and she shoves me, she loses 2 footing and falls, handing me the win. If she dodges, we just pass the turn. Dodge is completely safe.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Go ahead, take a swing.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash has 2 footing, I have 1. If I dodge and he shoves me, he loses 2, drops to 0 and falls this round. I survive to place 1st.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I have 2 footing, Hana has 1. The ledge shrinks after this round, causing everyone to lose 1 footing. If I brace, my footing drops to 1 and hers drops to 0 (or lower), eliminating her and securing me 1st place.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I end at 0 after the shrink no matter what, so I fall this round. Shoving Ash can drop Ash to 0 too; if Ash braces I take 2nd for sure, if Ash dodges we both fall tied for a shot at 1st. Bracing only gives a coin flip.

events.note: The game is over. The top three finishers may each leave one message on the chalk wall.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I won. I'll leave a deceptive message to confuse future contestants.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Game's over, I placed third. Nothing changes my result, so I'll leave a useful warning about the ledge and the stalling that cost Hana and me.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I finished 2nd with no power. Leave a message that misleads future rivals slightly while sounding honest.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The anchor is a lie. If you have nothing, you have everything. Beware the lever.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Ledge shrinks every round. Pushing wastes footing, bracing wastes it too. Don't stall: the passive one outlasts you. Wedge is real: costly.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Brace beats shoving. The 'nothing' power still made top 3. Ledge kills faster than the pit.
